title: Boots Castle takes him to hear Basie at the Reno Club
summary: A woman called Boots Castle guides him to the Reno Club on 12th Street, where he hears the Basie band with Lips Page, Buster Smith and Jimmy Rushing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, I was walking down the street on a Sunday night, and I met a girl who asked me what I was looking for and I said, 'music'.
Really?
That's what I was looking for!
Okay.
Well, this girl turned out to be -- her name was Boots Castle Dine. C-a-s-t-l-e D-i-n-e.
Uh huh.

But she went by the name Boots Castle. I'm getting ahead of myself here. And discovering that it was music, she guided me to the Reno Club and said after 12 o'clock the band starts, it was Monday morning, and little did I know, that they had what they called a breakfast dance.
Where was this Reno Club? Do you remember the street?
It was on 12th Street.
On 12th Street?
Sure I remember, it was 12th Street.
Was this black place or a white place, because you know in those days, in the 30's there were white and black places.
This was a little club -- it was a white place where ranchers would come in, but all they served was beer and chile.
To white folks?
Yes.
Of course.
But they had an all-black show.
Yeah, but black people couldn't come in.

I heard this band, and for a 15¢ beer, and almost fell on the floor. Now this was the first band that I heard, it was Basie, Joe Keys on trumpet, Oran "Lips" Page and a fellow called Rabbit who I heard with Fletcher Henderson, commited suicide, on trombone, and some people know his name, but I can't remember it, but they had a bass player with a Sousaphone, who wore a cap, it was a round shell, you know, with a big thing down there that said 'feed the kitty'.

But I heard this music, and they had a drummer whose name -- Buster Smith played first saxophone, and wrote the arrangements; Jackie Washington was playing saxophone -- he had three saxophones. And then they played the show; Jimmy Rushing was part of the show. Other names I have later on.
But I heard the music, and I couldn't believe it.
